FAIL-CLOSED, PROBED IN THE DIRECTION OF THE 'I could not check' DEFECT PATTERN. commit_files() runs git under check=True, so an unreadable sha raises rather than returning [] that would read as 'no files, therefore not record-only, therefore checked'. _is_record_only_commit returns False for an empty file list and False for a falsy pr_number. Every failure mode of the new exemption therefore lands on 'not exempt' (stricter), never on 'silently exempt'. This is the correct direction for an exemption.

FINDINGS -- non-blocking. None changes my verdict; recording them so they are not rediscovered.

F1. THE ONE MUTATION PROBE THAT WAS NOT CAUGHT: THE CLI WIRING IS UNTESTED. In scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py main(), I replaced 'findings = check(rev_range, args.pr_number)' with 'findings = check(rev_range, 0)' -- i.e. the new --pr-number flag parsed but thrown away, the entire feature inert at the command line -- and the full suite stayed at 534 passed, 0 failed. Every new identity test calls check() directly with an explicit pr_number and none goes through main()/argparse. The shipped behaviour is CORRECT (M5 proves the real CLI honours the flag), so this is a coverage gap, not a defect: today the only thing standing between 'the flag works' and 'the flag is decorative' is a manual run. One test that invokes main() with sys.argv, or asserts check() is called with args.pr_number, would close it. This is distinct from reviewer A's N1, which is about the 'if not pr_number: return False' guard inside _is_record_only_commit; mine is the argparse-to-check hand-off one level up.

F2. THE NEW EXEMPTION IS A NEW WRITE SURFACE, BY DESIGN, AND WORTH NAMING. Before this PR, lwb_check_commit_identity.py exempted nothing. After it, any git identity whatsoever can land a commit on PR N's branch touching only reviews/N/ without the identity gate looking at it -- including a commit that EDITS an existing reviewer's record, e.g. flipping a DISAGREE to AGREE. lwb_lanes.py still validates the record's contents (schema, id format, shared-segment, freshness), so the forged record would have to be internally well-formed, and it must still be pushed by someone with write access -- which is why I am not blocking. But the exemption is scoped by PATH only: M5's probe shows the gate accepting an identity it exists to reject, for a file under reviews/45/. Reviewer A's N3 notes the by-path/not-by-filename half of this; I am recording the write-surface half, which is the part that matters if branch protection ever loosens.

F3. THE HANDOFF PROOF COUNT CANNOT SURFACE A MISSING RECORD, ONLY AN INVALID ONE. lwb_handoff.py's generated line computes total = len(proof/*.json records present) and proven = those that validate, so '22/22 proven -- (all proven; none outstanding)' is 'every record I found is valid', not 'every deliverable has a record'. HANDOFF.md's own prose three paragraphs above says main is NOT green because #34 shipped with no proof/34.json -- and proof/ indeed has no 34.json. So the generated block reads 'none outstanding' on a branch whose base is missing a required record. This is the repo's own named defect pattern ('I could not check' sharing a representation with 'I checked and found nothing'), in the reporting layer. It is PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN -- the same shape produced '21/21 proven' before this PR -- and completeness is lwb-proof-coverage's job, which does run on push to main. This PR only regenerates the block, so this is NOT a #45 defect and I am not asking #45 to fix it. Recorded because a reader of HANDOFF.md is being told 'none outstanding' while the repo's own tip is red for exactly an outstanding record.

F4. PATH-PREFIX MATCHING IS NOT NORMALISED. _is_record_only_commit tests posix.startswith(f'reviews/{pr}/'), so a path literally spelled 'reviews/45/../../scripts/evil.py' would match. I checked whether this is reachable rather than reporting it as a hole: git's own plumbing normalises away '..' and refuses such paths in a tree, and commit_files reads git diff-tree output, so I could not construct one. Not exploitable as far as I could measure; noted only so the next reader does not have to redo that check.

NEAR-MISS I CAUGHT AND AM PRINTING, per the honesty rule. My first two attempts at the M5 end-to-end probe silently created NO commit -- 'git commit -am' does not add an untracked file, and my second attempt's 'git add' ran after a reset had already deleted the file. Both runs printed 'lwb-commit-identity check passed' for all three argument forms, which reads exactly like 'the exemption is inert and the flag does nothing'. I was one step from writing a DISAGREE finding that the --pr-number scoping does not actually discriminate. What saved it was printing the probe commit's author and file list instead of trusting that the commit happened: the line read '0de6776 LEAPWare ... files: reviews/45/cloud-reviewer-clock-01N9VKEa.json', i.e. still the branch head, no probe commit at all. The lesson I am recording: a probe that produces a PASS must first prove it changed something, or a no-op probe is indistinguishable from a passing one -- the very defect shape this repo asks reviewers to hunt, committed by the reviewer's own test harness.
